proof_audit.finding: Identification is injectivity within a complete maintained law or chosen moment map. Local rank is separated from global injectivity and calibration. The compact proof uses continuity, uniqueness, an attained positive gap, uniform error and an approximate-optimizer tolerance. Empty complement sets are treated explicitly.

Solve both equations on all 16 independent sign atoms. Derive reduced-form means and covariances and both OLS slopes. Tax shifts producer receipts only under the maintained law. The cost-only observational equivalence family belongs to a separate noiseless submodel; it does not preserve the richer joint law.

proof_audit.topic: Linear minimum distance and wrong-model target
proof_audit.finding: Positive weights and full column rank make G-prime W G positive definite. Completing the square proves a unique global projection even with nonzero residual. The Gaussian parameter covariance is exact for the unrestricted linear estimator.

The competitive output calculation is local to positive slope and price above intercept. The delta variance is asymptotic, not a finite Gaussian ratio variance. The perfectly fitted cubic perturbation has strictly positive marginal-cost derivative and a unique global price crossing; the whole kappa family remains observationally equivalent at the design points.

proof_audit.topic: Simulation coupling and fixed simulation floor
proof_audit.finding: Independent observation errors and explicit Gaussian simulation coefficients give two different exact variances. Common parameter-trial draws cancel the additive finite-difference noise, while a common row draw set survives N growth. The variance 5000 pertains to one R-draw simulator evaluation.

Four possible records yield a direct uniform frequency LLN on the compact positive-probability domain. Strict concavity plus exact expected score zero proves the wrong target. Bounded derivatives and the iid finite-support score CLT justify the sandwich only around that target.

All probabilities remain at least 1/20. Log contributions are 20-Lipschitz; Cauchy and Markov yield uniform discrepancy at most 4/sqrt(R) in expectation and consistency as R grows. At true probability 1/2, strict Jensen bias coexists with the correct target; differentiating its expected-score equation gives target slope 21/29. No generic rate or additional triangular-array inference theorem is adopted.

proof_audit.topic: Indirect inference exact covariance and boundaries
proof_audit.finding: The shared observed X cancels in D; it contributes cross covariance 1 between the auxiliary estimates. Explicit scalar-noise uniformity and global injectivity on [0,3] give consistency. The regular normal law assumes 0<theta0<3. Zero has the fourth-root positive-part limit; the upper endpoint has a clipped root-N limit. A sign-unrestricted map is globally many-to-one despite nonzero derivatives.

proof_audit.topic: Centered Gumbel and finite discounted dynamic choice
proof_audit.finding: Tail bounds establish the finite Gumbel mean. Multiplication of CDFs and integration derive expected max and softmax; subtracting the mean avoids the source normalization ambiguity. Monotonicity and translation prove the log-sum Lipschitz bound, finite-dimensional Cauchy convergence, uniqueness and the residual certificate.

proof_audit.topic: Dynamic observation law and inverse map
proof_audit.finding: The synthetic counts represent independent once-observed decision makers with fixed initial states. A trajectory instead needs sequential action/transition factors, with impossible transitions assigned zero probability. Given beta and normalization, the positive-rate inverse recovers r,c; unknown beta admits an equivalent family with different subsidy predictions.

proof_audit.topic: Implicit Bellman derivatives and error propagation
proof_audit.finding: The Jacobian beta P has a convergent Neumann inverse for beta<1. Accepted finite-dimensional implicit-function tools justify differentiation of the unique value. Values, log odds and choice derivatives are solved analytically and compared with finite differences of an independent scalar-ratio solver. Log probability error follows from two bounded index/log-sum differences; normalized utility is not dollar welfare.

An exactly specified population taste distribution yields the response map without a continuum iid assertion. Continuity proves existence; a strict global Lipschitz constant proves uniqueness for absolute b<4. The centered logit curve has exactly two critical points and known endpoint limits, proving all equilibrium counts and fold tangency. Implicit derivatives fail at the folds. Stability describes only the declared iteration. Randomized-selection mean sets are convex hulls; realized outcomes remain roots and the set is not a confidence interval.
